# An exact A=0 circuit obstruction to a per-group stress bound

This example satisfies all of the current normalized first-order cap and
shared-body-plane moment equations, but its single group has multiplier sum
larger than 1/gamma_2. It is not a depth minimizer. An explicit nearby depth
improvement is given below. Thus the missing use of actual extremality cannot
be replaced by these moment equations alone.

## 1. Body, projection and exact maximum depth

Let n=d=2 and put

    p1=(1,0), p2=(0,1), p3=(-1,-1), P={0,p1,p2,p3},
    T=conv{p1,p2,p3} in the continuous plane,
    C=conv(P) x T.

The integer points of conv(P)=T are exactly P. For instance the triangle
has area 3/2, its three primitive edges have no additional lattice points,
and its sole interior lattice point is 0 (equivalently one can check its
three inequalities directly). Write a=area(T)=3/2. Every fiber is T and the
mixed mass is M=4a. Put gamma=gamma_2=4/9.

Every point in an outer fiber has depth at most gamma/4: choose a triangle
cap of area at most gamma a through its continuous coordinate, and add a
sufficiently large integer-coordinate tilt exposing that outer vertex. This
excludes the other three fibers exactly. Conversely the triangle centroid
in that fiber has depth at least gamma/4 from its own fiber alone.

The central point y=(0,0) has depth exactly

    beta=(gamma+1)/4=13/36.

For the lower bound, consider an arbitrary closed ambient halfspace through
y. Its central-fiber section has area at least gamma a by the ordinary
triangle Grünbaum inequality. For the three outer sections, let R be the
linear area-preserving cyclic permutation of T's vertices. Then

    x+Rx+R^2 x=0,     p1+p2+p3=0.

Couple their uniform laws by the triples (p1,x),(p2,Rx),(p3,R^2x). Their
ambient sum is zero. At least one member of each triple lies in any closed
halfspace through zero. Integrating gives total outer cap area at least a.
The same conclusion holds for vertical normals, so the total is at least
(gamma+1)a. A halfspace containing y can first have its boundary shifted to
y, only decreasing its mass.

For the upper bound on EVERY point (0,x), choose a triangle halfspace through
x with area at most gamma a and use a large integer tilt to include one
outer fiber and exclude the other two. Such a tilt exists because each p_i
is strictly exposed among {p1,p2,p3} by a linear functional vanishing at 0.
This gives mass at most (gamma+1)a. Thus beta is the exact global maximum,
and the central integer index is the only globally deepest index.

## 2. A balanced critical cap group covering all ambient space

Set

    u1=(2,-1), u2=(-1,2), u3=(-1,-1),
    H_j={ (z,x): 10 u_j.z+u_j.x>=0 }.

One has sum_j u_j=0 and

    u_j.p_j=2,       u_j.p_i=-1 when i!=j,
    -1<=u_j.x<=2 for x in T.

Thus H_j contains its j-th outer fiber entirely and excludes both other
outer fibers. On the central fiber it is the vertex cap u_j.x>=0, of area
gamma a. Each cap has mass (gamma+1)a=beta M. Their margins sum to zero, so
the three CLOSED caps cover every point of the full ambient R^4.

The positive circuit weights can be taken as rho_j=1/3 with these
unnormalized normals. The common projected term is A=sum rho_j(10u_j)=0.
Every cap plane passes through y, and its only fiber section is the proper
central-triangle section through the centroid. Each such section has
continuous centroid 0. Consequently all full section centroids are y.

For formulas using unit continuous normals, replace each cap's coefficients
by their ratio to c_j=|u_j| and use rho_j=c_j/(c1+c2+c3). This is the same
positive circuit and the same three halfspaces. No non-unit normalization
is being silently inserted into unit-normal derivative formulas.

## 3. Exact normalized stress, including every body-facet first moment

Give every cap the same multiplier

    lambda_j=12/13.

Then sum lambda_j=36/13=1/beta, but

    36/13 - 1/gamma = 36/13-9/4=27/52>0.

Use the shared body inequalities u_l.x>=-1, l=1,2,3. Each is a facet plane
of all four fibers. Let F_l be the opposite edge to p_l, let L_l be its
length and let c_l be its edge centroid. There are no body-owner ties.
The total objective facet measure has

    mass 4 L_l, integer first moment 0,
    continuous first moment 4 L_l c_l.

The body trace of H_j on F_l consists of the entire j-th outer copy of F_l,
and, on the central copy, the subset F_l intersect {u_j.x>=0}. For j=l this
central subset is empty. For each of the two j!=l it is a segment of length
(2/3)L_l. Those two segments are exchanged by the affine reflection of the
edge about c_l. Their summed mass and first moment are therefore

    (4/3)L_l,       (4/3)L_l c_l.

Across all three caps, the outer full traces contribute mass 3L_l,
integer moment L_l(p1+p2+p3)=0, and continuous moment 3L_l c_l.
Multiplication by lambda=12/13 gives exactly

    (12/13)(3+4/3)L_l = 4L_l,
    integer moment 0,
    continuous moment 4L_l c_l.

Thus EACH shared body plane has zero signed zeroth and full first moments,
exactly as required by shared-ambient-facet-stress.md.

The cap-side equations also hold. In the unnormalized cap coordinates the
coarea section mass S_j=length(section_j)/|u_j| is the same for all j:

    area(T intersect {u_j.x>=t})=a ((2-t)/3)^2,
    S_j=4a/9 at t=0.

All section integer and continuous moments vanish. Assign the deepest index
0 to this group; one nonnegative coverage multiplier t can be chosen with
lambda S=(1/3)t. In unit coordinates the rescaled rho and S give the identical
equations. Added groups at nondeep outer fibers have slack budgets and zero
multipliers. The common-apex, deepest-support, positive-circuit, A=0,
coverage and exact Euler identities are all satisfied.

## 4. A strict improving variation exists through different active caps

The reason this is no counterexample to extremality is explicit. Let the
outer fibers be r_i T and keep the central fiber T, with

    r1=1-t, r2=1, r3=1+t,       0<t<=1/4.

There is an affine scalar function r(z) with these values on the three outer
vertices and r(0)=1. The shared inequalities u_l.x>=-r(z) define precisely
these four fibers, so this is a valid nearby convex deformation with the
same three shared body planes and central volume normalization.

More generally, for any positive r_i of mean1, put r_min=min r_i and
r_max=max r_i. The exact maximum depth of this homothetic family is

    max{ gamma r_max^2, gamma+r_min^2 }/(1+sum_i r_i^2).

Indeed each outer vertex fiber can be isolated, giving its exact maximum
gamma r_i^2 divided by the total. For the central fiber, the common smaller
triangle r_min T in every outer fiber and the cyclic coupling prove the
lower bound gamma+r_min^2 at the central centroid. For the matching upper
bound at any central point, take its triangle cap of area at most gamma a
and an integer tilt isolating the smallest outer fiber.

For the stated small t, the central term dominates, and the new maximum is

    beta(t)=(13/9-2t+t^2)/(4+2t^2) < 13/36,

since the positive difference has numerator 2t-(5/18)t^2. The original fixed
three cap budgets do not allow this deformation: the cap containing the
expanded outer fiber increases. Alternative critical caps, all selecting
the newly smallest outer fiber, do give the decrease in actual depth.

Hence a first-order certificate based on one arbitrary compressed critical
cover can satisfy every available balance equation at a non-minimizer.
Actual extremality must also control alternative active cap selections.
